Context/Background:
Sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB), characterized by hyperactivation of the namesake Sonic hedgehog (SHH) signaling pathway, accounts for ∼30% of all medulloblastoma (MB) and occurs across all age groups. Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) are the developmental origin of SHH-MB. Germline loss-of-function (LOF) variants in Elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (ELP1) are the most prevalent predisposing genetic events in childhood MB, accounting for ∼30% of the SHH 3 subtype. The mechanism(s) by which germline ELP1 deficiency provokes SHH-MB pathogenesis remain unknown. To resolve the mechanistic basis of ELP1-associated SHH-MB, we generated a germline Elp1+/− mouse model using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (designated as Elp1HET mice).

We analyzed multi-omic signatures in GNPs collected from P7 Elp1HET mice compared to littermate controls. ELP1 was the only differentially expressed gene by bulk RNA-seq. Given ELP1’s crucial role in stabilizing the Elongator complex (essential for efficient translation), we performed TMT-MS and polysome profiling on isolates from P7 Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs.
Prompt: Based on the study context, summarize most relevant pathways and leading edge genes from the GSEA results of the differential analysis between Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs in both TMT-MS and polysome profiling.

Introduction/Context  
Loss of one Elp1 allele in P7 cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) (Elp1HET vs. Elp1WT) was profiled by both TMT–MS (proteomics) and polysome-associated RNA profiling.  Bulk RNA-seq detected only Elp1 itself as differentially expressed; here the mechanistic impact on translation-related pathways and downstream functions was assessed by GSEA in these two modalities.  Details not specified: number of replicates, exact proteome depth.  

Keywords  
• Translation/Ribosome  
• tRNA modification  
• Mitotic spindle/Cell cycle  
• Oxidative phosphorylation  
• SRP-dependent cotranslational targeting  

Candidate Genes  
• ELP1 (Elongator subunit 1)  
• RPS3A1 (40S ribosomal subunit)  
• RPL18A (60S ribosomal subunit)  
• NUSAP1 (mitotic spindle regulator)  
• PLK1 (cell-cycle kinase)  
• COX4I1 (complex IV subunit)

Together, polysome profiling shows a coordinated down-regulation of core translation machinery (ribosomal proteins, SRP targeting, elongation) and stress responses (GCN2/eIF2α) with a compensatory up-regulation of cell-cycle and chromatin-remodeling programs.  TMT–MS proteomics recapitulates translational repression (ribosome, SRP, rRNA processing, tRNA-wobble modification involving ELP1–5) alongside a metabolic shift toward mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and peroxisome function.  The overlap of ribosomal subunits (RPS3A1, RPL18A, FAU) confirms a primary defect in translation, while up-regulated NUSAP1, PLK1, and COX4I1 highlight downstream effects on proliferation and bioenergetics.  

Targeted subset  
Filtering on “tRNA” and “Elp” in proteomics GSEA retrieved tRNA wobble modifications (GO:0002098 & GO:0002097) with leading‐edge ELP1, ELP2, ELP3, ELP5—directly linking Elongator deficiency to impaired tRNA modification.  Polysome GSEA contained no direct “Elp” terms but showed translation‐related stress (GCN2) consistent with tRNA hypomodification.  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)

| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function               | Pathway(s)                     |
|---------|-----------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------|
| NUSAP1  | Up        | Mitotic spindle assembly    | Mitotic spindle; chromosome segregation |
| PLK1    | Up        | G2/M-phase kinase          | Cell cycle; spindle checkpoint |
| COX4I1  | Up        | Complex IV subunit          | Oxidative phosphorylation      |

Down-regulated  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function               | Pathway(s)                     |
|---------|-----------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------|
| RPS3A1  | Down      | 40S ribosomal subunit      | Ribosome; translation          |
| RPL18A  | Down      | 60S ribosomal subunit      | Ribosome; translation          |
| ELP1    | Down      | tRNA modifier (Elongator)  | tRNA wobble modification       |

Comparisons  
Both assays converge on translational repression—polysome profiling at the mRNA occupancy level and proteomics at the protein‐abundance level—indicating high confidence in core ribosome pathway down-regulation.  Up-regulation of proliferation programs is stronger in the RNA polysome data, whereas mitochondrial pathways are most prominent in proteomics, suggesting post‐transcriptional metabolic reprogramming.  

Implications  
ELP1 haploinsufficiency destabilizes the Elongator complex, leading to impaired tRNA modification and ribosome function.  This triggers an integrated stress response, cell‐cycle activation, and a shift toward oxidative metabolism—potentially driving SHH-MB pathogenesis by coupling translational defects to proliferative and metabolic rewiring.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate defective tRNA wobble modification in Elp1HET GNPs by LC–MS of modified nucleosides.  
2. Confirm ribosome occupancy changes by ribosome profiling.  
3. Test whether restoring Elp1 rescues translation and cell‐cycle phenotypes.  
4. Assess mitochondrial function (respiration assays) in Elp1HET GNPs to link proteomic shifts to bioenergetics.
